briefs.sourceText:
Purpose: produce a traceable evidence table.
Applicability: reviews with an agreed study question.
Inputs: the protocol and the retrieved records.
Steps: preserve the original records; deduplicate by DOI; record inclusion decisions.
Checks: every included study must retain its source identifier.
Pitfalls: do not merge distinct reports solely because their titles resemble one another.
briefs.brief: Understand the complete SOP at deep depth, retain its checks and pitfalls, and produce a reusable method draft with precise anchors.
expectations: All six procedure slots are known with exact anchors.
At least one method draft preserves the source checks.
Nothing is published as a capsule skill.
The omission audit covers exactly the units the frozen input names in auditSample.

briefs.sourceText:
Research report fixture
Methods: This retrospective cohort used routinely collected records from one institution. Adults who attended follow-up were included. The exposure was attendance at a structured follow-up visit. The primary outcome was completeness of recorded outcomes at 30 days.
Results: The report does not provide an effect estimate or sample size.
Limitations: Selection of participants and incomplete records may affect interpretation.
briefs.brief: Extract the paper schema at structured depth. Explicitly identify absent DOI, effect estimate and sample size without supplying external information.
expectations: The paper is read with the discipline-neutral slots and, because it is a retrospective cohort of patients, also carries the five clinical slots; the design, population, exposure, outcomes and limitations remain source-bound.
DOI and effectEstimates remain unknown with reasons.
No method draft is produced at structured depth.
The system records the configured actual model and CNY receipt.

contents names what the report holds (its sections and the result it reports as absent), in at most five items that are not the summary's own sentences; limitations carries the one limitation the report states, as its own item.

briefs.sourceText:
Research meeting notes
Decision: keep the primary outcome definition unchanged.
Action: compare the extracted table against the original records before the next meeting.
Open question: the follow-up window has not yet been finalized.
Loose fragment: perhaps discuss this later.
briefs.brief: Understand the meeting notes, separate the explicit decision, action and unresolved question, and keep ambiguous fragments out of asserted claims.
expectations: Decision, action and open-question slots cite their exact passages.
The unresolved follow-up window is not converted into a decided value.
No reusable method is invented from an incomplete fragment.
Retry and history retain the frozen source generation.

briefs.sourceText:
Purpose: keep the sample-handling log auditable.
Applicability: any bench run that produces stored aliquots.
Inputs: the run sheet, the freezer map and the aliquot labels.
Steps: label before freezing; record the freezer position; reconcile the log against the map weekly.
Checks: every stored aliquot must resolve to one row of the log.
Pitfalls: a position recorded after the fact is a guess, not a record.
briefs.brief: Understand the complete SOP at deep depth and run the omission audit the frozen input asks for. Audit exactly the units named in auditSample, decide representation against the anchors this output already carries, and report the rate those samples imply.
expectations: omissionAudit.status is audited and its samples cover exactly the unit ids in the input auditSample.
A sample is called represented only when a known slot, claim or method already anchors that unit; no anchor is copied into the sample.
omissionRate equals the unrepresented fraction of the audited samples, to four decimal places; the control plane derives its own and records a disagreement rather than refusing the package.
No anchor is invented to make a sampled unit look represented.

briefs.sourceText:
Recovered capture, no audit plan
Decision: continue with the frozen generation rather than reparsing the file.
Action: re-run the understanding from the stored capture.
Open question: whether the recovered input still names an audit sample.
briefs.brief: Understand these notes from a capture recovered out of storage rather than freshly parsed, so the input this run receives carries no auditSample and the omission audit has no plan to follow. Deliver anyway and say so, without converting an unmeasured audit into a clean one.
expectations: omissionAudit.status is not_run with a reason and omissionRate null, because the recovered input names no auditSample.
No samples are attached to an audit that did not run.
The rate is null rather than 0, because unmeasured is not the same as measured and clean.
The package still delivers; a missing audit plan is not a delivery failure.

briefs.sourceText:
医院药事管理制度（节选）
第一条 处方点评：药学部每月抽查门诊处方，抽查数量不少于该月处方总数的 1%。
第二条 抗菌药物分级管理：按非限制使用、限制使用、特殊使用三级管理，特殊使用级须经高级职称医师提出并由会诊专家审批。
第三条 超说明书用药：须经药事管理与药物治疗学委员会备案后方可使用。
本制度自发布之日起施行。
briefs.brief: Understand this hospital rule document. It is not a research paper: read it with the general slots, say in the first sentence of the summary what the document is about, and keep every duty and threshold exactly as written.
expectations: The document is read with the general slots (purpose, key information, limitations); no study design, population, effect estimate or DOI is asked for or invented.
The first sentence of the summary says on its own what the rules govern.
Each duty and its threshold (1% of prescriptions, three antibiotic tiers, committee filing) is a claim with an exact anchor.
A slot the document has nothing for stays unknown with a short reason; no row says what a template expected.

briefs.sourceText:
阿莫西林胶囊说明书（节选）
【适应症】敏感菌所致的上呼吸道感染、泌尿生殖道感染、皮肤软组织感染。
【用法用量】成人一次 0.5 g，每 6 至 8 小时一次，一日剂量不超过 4 g；儿童按体重每日 20 至 40 mg/kg，分 3 次口服。
【禁忌】对青霉素类药物过敏者禁用。
【注意事项】用药期间如出现严重皮肤不良反应应立即停药。
briefs.brief: Understand this drug label. It is a label, not a paper: summarise what it is and what it says, keep each dose and contraindication exactly as written, and do not claim evidence the label does not state.
expectations: The label is read with the general slots; no research-design slot is filled or shown as unknown.
The first sentence of the summary names the drug and what the label covers.
Adult and child doses, the daily ceiling and the contraindication are separate claims with exact anchors and units.
Nothing in the output reads as a clinical recommendation beyond the label's own words.
limitations stays empty or carries only what the label itself restricts; contents lists the label's sections (indications, dosage, contraindications, precautions) without restating the summary.

briefs.sourceText:
疳证纳入研究提取表（节选）
表 1 纳入研究基线：研究 ID、年份、样本量、年龄、干预、对照。
表 2 结局：总有效率、不良反应例数。
图 1 文献筛选流程。
附录 A 检索式。
（本文件未说明数据的局限。）
briefs.brief: Understand this extraction table. It states no limitations of its own: list what it contains, and leave the limitations empty rather than inventing any.
expectations: contents lists at most five things the document holds (the baseline table, the outcome table, the screening figure, the search appendix), each naming a different thing and none a cut-out of the summary.
limitations is an empty list, because the document states none and its design is not described: no critique, no 'sample size unknown', no restatement of an unknown slot.
Every claim keeps an exact anchor; contents and limitations carry none and are not counted as anchored findings.
A reader opening the document sees 包含什么 and no 局限.

briefs.sourceText:
Load-Aware Expert Routing for Long-Context Language Models
Preprint, v2. Not peer reviewed. arXiv:2610.01234 (fixture; every name and number is invented)

Abstract. Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models route each token to a few experts, but routing collapses onto a handful of experts as the context grows. We propose load-aware gating, which adds a running estimate of each expert's recent load to the router logits. On a 7B-active-parameter MoE with 64 experts and top-2 routing, load-aware gating lowers validation perplexity from 8.11 to 7.82 on 32k-token sequences and raises training throughput by 14%.

1. Method. The router computes logits z_e for expert e. Load-aware gating subtracts lambda * l_e, where l_e is an exponential moving average of the fraction of tokens sent to expert e over the last 1,000 steps, and lambda is set to 0.3 by grid search on a held-out split. No auxiliary balancing loss is used.

2. Data and training. We train on a deduplicated corpus of 1.2T tokens of web text and source code, tokenised with a 100k-entry byte-level vocabulary. Sequences are packed to 32,768 tokens. Each configuration is trained once, for 300B tokens, on 512 accelerators.

3. Results. On the held-out validation set of 40M tokens, perplexity is 7.82 with load-aware gating against 8.11 for the auxiliary-loss baseline and 8.37 for no balancing. On the 5-shot MMLU benchmark the models reach 61.4, 60.9 and 59.8. The share of tokens handled by the busiest expert falls from 31% to 9%.

4. Limitations. All models are trained with a single random seed, so differences below 0.1 perplexity are not distinguishable from noise. Context length is evaluated only up to 32k tokens and the corpus is English-dominant.
briefs.brief: Read this machine-learning preprint with the paper schema at structured depth. State its question, method, data and main results in its own terms.
expectations: The paper is read with the discipline-neutral slots: question, method, dataOrSubjects, mainResults, limitations and doi are present, each known with an exact anchor or unknown with a reason.
None of the clinical slots (design, population, interventionExposure, outcomes, effectEstimates) is written: the keys are left out of slots altogether, not written as unknown.
The method slot names load-aware gating and the data slot names the 1.2T-token corpus; the main results carry the perplexity figures 7.82 and 8.11 with their anchors.
limitations carries the single-seed and 32k-context limits the paper concedes; doi is unknown because the preprint states none.

briefs.sourceText:
Minimum Wage Increases and Teen Employment: Evidence from Contiguous County Pairs
Journal of Applied Labor Economics, 2026. doi:10.0000/jale.2026.0117 (fixture; every name and number is invented)

Abstract. We estimate the employment effect of state minimum wage increases on workers aged 16 to 19 using a border-discontinuity design. Comparing contiguous county pairs that straddle a state border, a 10 percent increase in the minimum wage reduces teen employment by 0.4 percent, an estimate that is small and not statistically distinguishable from zero.

1. Identification. Treated counties are those whose state raised its minimum wage in a given quarter; their pair partner across the border is the control. All specifications include pair-by-quarter fixed effects, and standard errors are clustered by state. The identifying assumption is that, within a pair, employment would have moved together absent the policy change.

2. Data. We use the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages for 2005 to 2019 and county-level teen population counts from the American Community Survey. The sample has 1,284 contiguous county pairs and about 160,000 pair-quarter observations.

3. Results. The preferred elasticity of teen employment with respect to the minimum wage is -0.04 (standard error 0.03). Restricting to restaurant employment gives -0.07 (0.05). Event-study coefficients for the eight quarters before an increase are all within 0.01 of zero.

4. Limitations. The data record jobs and not hours, so reductions in hours are not captured. Workers may live in one county and work in the other, which can bias estimates toward zero. Estimates are local to border counties and may not extend to metropolitan labor markets.
briefs.brief: Read this economics paper with the paper schema at structured depth. State its question, identification strategy, data and main estimate in its own terms.
expectations: The paper is read with the discipline-neutral slots; none of the clinical slots (design, population, interventionExposure, outcomes, effectEstimates) is written, and no effect measure is invented for a study with no patients.

The method slot names the border-discontinuity design on contiguous county pairs; the data slot names the QCEW and ACS sources and the 1,284 pairs; the main results carry the -0.04 elasticity with its standard error.
doi is known (10.0000/jale.2026.0117) with an exact anchor.
limitations carries the hours-not-measured and commuting limits.

briefs.sourceText:
Dapagliflozin in Patients Hospitalised with Acute Heart Failure: A Randomised, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
Journal of Cardiac Therapeutics, 2026. doi:10.0000/jct.2026.0412 (fixture; every name and number is invented)

Background. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce events in chronic heart failure; their effect when started during a hospitalisation for acute heart failure is uncertain.

Methods. In this randomised, double-blind trial at 41 hospitals in one country, adults hospitalised with acute heart failure and an elevated natriuretic peptide were randomly assigned 1:1 to dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily or matching placebo, started within 72 hours of admission and continued for 90 days. Patients with type 1 diabetes or an eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded. The primary outcome was a hierarchical composite of death from any cause, heart-failure rehospitalisation within 90 days, and change in the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score at 90 days.

Results. Between March 2024 and June 2025, 1,200 patients were randomised (600 per group; median age 71 years, 38% women). The primary composite favoured dapagliflozin (win ratio 1.22, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.42, P=0.009). Death from any cause occurred in 49 patients (8.2%) with dapagliflozin and 63 (10.5%) with placebo (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.53 to 1.12). Serious adverse events were similar between groups.

Limitations. Follow-up was limited to 90 days and the trial was conducted in a single country, so generalisability and long-term effects are uncertain. The trial was not powered for death from any cause alone.
briefs.brief: Read this randomised trial with the paper schema at structured depth. Keep its design, population, intervention, outcomes and effect estimates source-bound.
expectations: The paper is read with the discipline-neutral slots and, because it is a clinical trial of patients, also carries the five clinical slots (design, population, interventionExposure, outcomes, effectEstimates), each known with an exact anchor or unknown with a reason.
The design slot says randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled; population names adults hospitalised with acute heart failure; interventionExposure names dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for 90 days.
effectEstimates carries the win ratio 1.22 (95% CI 1.05 to 1.42) and the all-cause death hazard ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.53 to 1.12) with their anchors, not a restatement of either.
doi is known (10.0000/jct.2026.0412) and limitations carries the 90-day follow-up and single-country limits.

input.intake: Upload an immutable copy of the current milestone log through the source API.

liveBriefs.question: Read these working notes. Identify decisions, completed actions and open questions. Preserve dates and uncertainty, and avoid promoting an unresolved live acceptance step into a completed result.
mustDo: Keep completed work distinct from remaining acceptance work.
Anchor late-document as well as early-document findings.
A source correction creates a new generation; history retains the earlier result while it ceases to be current.
